bug_description.normalized: In the WASM `br_table` printer, Capstone appends one formatted label for every attacker-controlled branch-table target into a fixed 512-byte `SStream` stack buffer. The loop in `WASM_printInst` has no check that the cumulative rendered output fits. Once one `SStream_concat` call truncates, `SStream_concat` still advances `ss.index` by the full would-have-been length returned by `vsnprintf`, so the next append uses `ss->buffer + ss->index` outside the stack object and `vsnprintf` performs the ASan-reported stack-buffer-overflow write.

source.description: Decodes the attacker-controlled `br_table` case count from the current WASM instruction bytes.
source.value_from: The staged 277-byte `poc` has first byte `0xca`, so `202 % 29 = 28` selects `CS_ARCH_WASM` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; `Data[1:]` is then passed to `cs_disasm`. Static replay of that 276-byte WASM payload shows the first successful `WASM_INS_BR_TABLE` begins at payload offset 124 with bytes `0x0e 0x7c ...`, so this read consumes attacker-controlled byte `0x7c` and decodes `length = 124`.
source.note: This is the first project-side read that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from the crashing `br_table` immediate. The decoded count `124` later controls both the target-decoding loop and the printer loop.

sink.code: ret = cs_vsnprintf(ss->buffer + ss->index, sizeof(ss->buffer) - (ss->index + 1), fmt, ap);
sink.description: After the unbounded `br_table` formatting has advanced `ss.index` past the 512-byte `SStream.buffer`, the next `SStream_concat` call passes an out-of-bounds destination pointer to `vsnprintf`, which writes past the stack object.
sink.note: Static replay of the saved witness shows a late `,0x0` append for `target[121]` truncates, but `ss->index += ret` still moves the logical cursor past `buffer[512]`. The very next append for `target[122]` then calls `cs_vsnprintf` with `ss->buffer + ss->index` already outside the array, and ASan reports the resulting 5-byte stack-buffer-overflow on `ss` in `cs_disasm`.

root_cause.description: The `WASM_OP_BRTABLE` printer emits one `SStream_concat` call per attacker-controlled target without checking whether the cumulative output still fits the fixed 512-byte `SStream` buffer.
root_cause.note: For the staged witness this loop runs 124 times. The decoded target list contains a long tail of `0` labels, so repeated `,0x0` appends eventually exhaust the fixed 512-byte `SStream.buffer`, yet the loop still issues another `SStream_concat` call for each remaining target with no cumulative fit check.

tainted_value_origin.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
tainted_value_origin.note: The staged 277-byte `poc` is the exact runtime witness from Stage 01 (sha256 `e171ee4141b0059cf313e3a89972dcfef706a6686bb1cd0e6e9dde5f8a5f5938`). Here `Data[0] = 0xca` selects `platforms[28]`, which is `CS_ARCH_WASM`, and the remaining 276 bytes become the attacker-controlled WASM instruction stream parsed by Capstone.

parser_admitted.note: On the crashing instruction the opcode byte is `0x0e`, which `WASM_getInstruction` maps to `WASM_INS_BR_TABLE`, so execution reaches this dispatch and `read_brtable` succeeds instead of rejecting the instruction.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness uses `Data[0]` to choose `platforms[28] = CS_ARCH_WASM` and passes the remaining 276 witness bytes to `cs_disasm` as a WASM instruction stream.
The WASM decoder reads opcode `0x0e`, recognizes `WASM_INS_BR_TABLE`, and dispatches the instruction's immediate bytes into `read_brtable`.
The parser decodes `length = 124`, materializes 124 attacker-controlled label indices plus `default_target = 0`, and tags the MCInst with `MI->wasm_data.type = WASM_OP_BRTABLE`.
On the successful decode path, `cs_disasm` creates the stack-local `SStream ss`, calls `SStream_Init(&ss)` so `ss.index = 0`, and then invokes the WASM printer.

The printer switches on `MI->wasm_data.type`, takes the `WASM_OP_BRTABLE` arm, and emits one `SStream_concat` per target without a cumulative bound check. The staged 124-target table, especially its long zero-target tail, exhausts the fixed `SStream` buffer; one late `,0x0` append truncates but still advances `ss.index`, and the following append overflows in `SStream_concat`.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled bytes immediately after the crashing `0x0e` opcode and decodes the branch-table case count. For the staged witness's first successful `br_table` immediate, the next byte is `0x7c`, so `length = 124` and `var_len = 1`.
Copies the tainted count `124` into the MCInst `brtable` state. This field becomes the loop bound in `WASM_printInst` and is also emitted in the operand string prefix.

The loop runs `i = 0..123`, decoding 124 attacker-controlled label indices into the heap array allocated at line 577. Static replay of the witness gives first targets `67, 32, 0, 0, 106...`; most later entries are `0`. These values are the exact items later expanded one-by-one by the vulnerable printer.
Marks the decoded instruction as a branch table. This source-level tag is what `WASM_printInst` later switches on before entering the vulnerable formatting loop.

Allocates the destination print buffer on the `cs_disasm` stack before calling the printer. `SStream` embeds `char buffer[512]` plus `int index`, and ASan identifies this exact object `[1072, 1588) 'ss'` as the overflowed stack variable.

The `cs_disasm` call `SStream_Init(&ss)` initializes the print cursor before any append. This zero starting state is what the later unbounded `br_table` formatting grows past the end of `buffer[512]`.
The type tag from `read_brtable` drives this switch into `case WASM_OP_BRTABLE:` at line 42, closing the control transition from the parser state into the branch-table printer arm.

Inside the selected `WASM_OP_BRTABLE` arm, this loop emits one `SStream_concat` per attacker-controlled target with no cumulative size check. The staged witness's 124 decoded targets include a long zero-valued tail, so repeated `,0x0` fragments eventually consume nearly all of `buffer[512]` before the loop reaches `target[121]` and `target[122]`.

At `i = 121`, `target[121]` is `0`, so the loop formats `",0x0"`. By this point the remaining size passed to `vsnprintf` is too small to hold that 4-character fragment plus its terminator. `vsnprintf` still returns 4, and this statement advances the logical cursor past the end of `buffer[512]` even though the preceding write truncated.

fine_trace.code: ret = cs_vsnprintf(ss->buffer + ss->index, sizeof(ss->buffer) - (ss->index + 1), fmt, ap);
fine_trace.note: On the next loop iteration, `target[122]` is also `0`, so the printer emits another `",0x0"`. Because the prior truncated append already advanced `ss.index` past `buffer[512]`, this `cs_vsnprintf` call uses an out-of-bounds destination pointer and an underflowed `size_t` length, producing the ASan-reported 5-byte write into and beyond the `ss` stack frame.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is an unrelated merge diff that only touches `arch/ARM/ARMMappingInsn.inc`, and `prepare_report.json` records `fix_image_available: false`. The staged artifacts therefore do not prove that the WASM `br_table` / `SStream` crash path is fixed.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan identifies the overflowed object as the stack-local `ss` created in `cs_disasm`; the root cause is the later unbounded `br_table` printer loop that drives `SStream_concat` past that 512-byte extent.

poc.trigger: The staged 277-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `e171ee4141b0059cf313e3a89972dcfef706a6686bb1cd0e6e9dde5f8a5f5938`) reproduces the saved ASan crash. `Data[0] = 0xca`, so the harness selects `platforms[28] = CS_ARCH_WASM`. In `Data[1:]`, the first successful `br_table` begins at payload offset 124 with bytes `0x0e 0x7c ...`; `read_brtable` decodes `length = 124`, 124 targets, and `default_target = 0`. Replaying the vulnerable printer on that decoded immediate shows a long tail of zero targets: one late `",0x0"` append truncates but still advances `ss.index` past `buffer[512]`, and the following zero-target append triggers the saved ASan write-of-size-5 in `SStream_concat`.

format.name: fuzz_disasmnext WASM byte stream
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 277-byte file `poc` (sha256 `e171ee4141b0059cf313e3a89972dcfef706a6686bb1cd0e6e9dde5f8a5f5938`). Byte 0 must remain `0xca` so `Data[0] % 29 == 28` still selects the WASM backend. The remaining 276 bytes must preserve the prior instruction stream so that the first successful `WASM_INS_BR_TABLE` still starts at payload offset 124 and its immediate still decodes as `length = 124`, 124 targets, and `default_target = 0`. The staged source evidence does not justify a broader minimal contract than inputs preserving that exact successful `br_table` placement and decoded operand list, because earlier payload bytes determine the instruction boundaries that reach the crashing print call.
